bullets.title: META: Muse AI agent hits #1 App Store; AMZN blocks; SHOP/PYPL/EXPE partner
bullets.body: META Muse reached #1 in US App Store downloads 9–13 days post-launch (2.5–3.1M downloads, 640–725K DAU), outpacing ChatGPT's equivalent launch metrics. Amazon blocked Muse from shopping on its platform citing unauthorized access and credential harvesting; Shopify CEO announced agentic checkout integration via Shop Pay, and PayPal/Expedia also announced Muse partnerships. JPM raised META PT to $920, Piper to $875, MS reiterates OW Top Pick at $775; Oppenheimer stays Perform noting subscription monetization adds only 4% to 2027 revenue even under heroic assumptions.

bullets.title: AKAM surges 15–23% on landmark $11.6B Anthropic deal; CIS segment re-rated
bullets.body: Akamai announced a seven-year, $11.6B take-or-pay CPU-based cloud infrastructure deal with Anthropic (expandable to ~$20B), warranting a 5% equity stake. No revenue before late 2027 but ramp to ~$1.7B annual run-rate by end-2028; capex ~$5.5B over two years. JP Morgan raised PT to $167 (Neutral, concentration risk), Oppenheimer reiterates OW at $180, D.A. Davidson initiates Buy at $185; Piper raised to OW noting CIS segment could surpass Security segment by 4Q28.

bullets.title: NVDA: CEO NDR bullish; Colossus 2 doubling GPU orders; forward P/E at decade lows
bullets.body: MS reports SPCX Colossus 2 may double NVDA GPU orders QoQ (~660K incremental chips, ~$18B, 15–20% of current quarterly revenue). NVDA forward P/E sits at ~15.75–17x, near decade lows. CEO Jensen Huang states AI chips will sell 'twice as many next year' following ~70% FY28 revenue guidance; Citi maintains Buy at 9x 2028 EPS. NVDA added to Hedgeye/Signal Strength bullish trend list.

bullets.title: AMD hits $1T market cap; INTC +12% on agentic AI CPU demand surge
bullets.body: AMD reached $1 trillion market cap for the first time, closing above $600 (post-split). INTC surged ~12–14% alongside ARM +14–17% as markets repriced CPU demand: agentic AI requires 3–4 CPUs per GPU vs 7–8 during training, driving exponential inference-era CPU demand. TSMC confirmed Intel Xeon 6 as host CPU for DGX Rubin NVL8. AMD and INTC showed highest bullish options flow of the day; AMD joins OpenAI/Meta 'warrants' already in the money.

bullets.title: ORCL: force majeure on Project Jupiter raises data center execution risk
bullets.body: Oracle sent force majeure notice to Blue Owl Capital on 2.45GW Project Jupiter (New Mexico) after natural gas pipeline permits denied twice; project debt trading below 90¢ on dollar. Oracle states project remains on schedule; force majeure is precautionary. Morgan Stanley turns cautious on credit; Bloom Energy confirms $1.25B EBITDA exposure but has take-or-pay contractual protections. KeyBanc reiterates OW at $300 PT; Mizuho maintains Outperform citing ORCL's broader 850MW+ delivered capacity and October 28 Investor Day.

bullets.title: MU: earnings Sept 30; street consensus $31.52 EPS / $50.97B revenue; bullish setup
bullets.body: Micron reports Wednesday Sept 30 after market. UBS models through-cycle EPS $212–$277 well above street, citing DRAM fulfillment at ~60% of demand with server DDR demand +80% YoY. Memory spot prices rising (DDR5 +5% M/M); HBM supply-demand shortage through 2028; Chips Act buyback restrictions expire Dec 9. ITC institutes investigation against MU for DRAM patent infringement (NLST case). Michael Burry increased short position.

bullets.title: CMCSA downgraded to Underweight at KeyBanc (PT $18) and MS cuts PT to $27
bullets.body: KeyBanc cut CMCSA to Underweight (PT $18, ~19% downside) citing accelerating broadband losses to fiber/FWA/Starlink, unwillingness to match $30–40/month competitor pricing, and NBCU spin as non-catalyst. Morgan Stanley cut PT from $29 to $27; expects 3Q broadband net adds of -140K to -160K vs consensus -119K. CHTR also cut to $140 from $150. TMUS remains top pick as least exposed to agentic AI ARPU risk.

bullets.title: PSKY/WBD: antitrust settlement clears; deal closes in ~2 weeks
bullets.body: California and state AGs settled antitrust challenge to Paramount-Skydance-WBD deal: no forced divestitures, 30–32 films/year commitment, $1.5B US production spend over 5 years, $47.5M worker fund, independent editorial boards for CNN/CBS. MS raised PSKY PT to $11.50, reiterates OW; sees path to >240M combined subs and $6B+ synergies. WBD +7–11% on the news; deal expected to close within 2 weeks avoiding ticking fee (~$7M/day from Oct 1).

bullets.title: MRVL: Morgan Stanley raises PT to $268; Investor Day Oct 6 could reveal $40B+ 2030 revenue target
bullets.body: MS raised MRVL PT from $246 to $268 citing AI upside; expects FY2030 revenue guidance to be raised to $40B+ at Oct 6 Investor Day driven by Google custom silicon and scale-up network demand. MRVL interconnect revenue tracking >70% YoY vs prior 50% expectation. Celestial AI acquisition includes $2B AWS purchase order; 1.6T speed tightness driving substitution into 800G.

bullets.title: DKNG: MA/MI regulators examine AI use; Predictions spend raised to $400-500M cutting EBITDA 20%
bullets.body: Massachusetts gambling regulator announced investigation into how DraftKings and other betting companies use AI. Oppenheimer revises Predictions investment upward to $400–500M from $200–300M, reducing 2026E EBITDA 20% to $548M from prior $700–900M guidance; core handle tracking +15% YoY for September, NFL season proceeding well. Stock has underperformed S&P by 20% since late August.

bullets.title: TSEM: Mizuho initiates Outperform at $300 PT; silicon photonics 60% CAGR to $8.5B by 2029
bullets.body: Mizuho initiated TSEM at Outperform with $300 PT (0.6x FY27 PEG, below peers' 0.9x). RF Infrastructure revenue projected at $3.8B by F29E (76% CAGR), with gross margin expanding 23% to 50% and EPS growing ~7x. SiPho foundry market growing 60% CAGR to $8.5B by 2029. TSEM +2.8–3.4% in premarket; Wells Fargo also initiated VRT at Overweight.

bullets.title: FOXA/ROKU: Q1 preview bullish; Fox-Roku deal expected regulatory approval 1H27
bullets.body: UBS raises FOXA F1Q Tubi estimate to +25% YoY on viewership lift; expects ~$1.37B EBITDA (+30% YoY), ~35% total ad growth. FY27 EBITDA guidance unchanged at $4.1B on World Cup knockout, elections, improving cable renewals. Wedbush sees $400M+ cost synergies from Fox-Roku deal expected to close 1H27; Fox stock trades at ~5.5x '28 standalone EV/EBITDA.

bullets.title: IONQ: quantum milestone at NVIDIA partnership; Superion 256 installed at NVAQC
bullets.body: IonQ's Superion 256 QPU will debut at NVIDIA's Accelerated Quantum Research Center, linked to GB200 NVL72 via NVQLink and orchestrated through CUDA-Q. IonQ also announced multi-year strategic collaboration with Korean SDT Inc. for Superion 256 supply. Separately, IonQ demonstrated real-time quantum error decoder, boosting shares +11–12% in premarket trading.

bullets.title: CRWV: JPM upgrades to OW; GPU pricing +25%, margins expanding toward 20%+
bullets.body: JPM upgraded CoreWeave to Overweight (PT $125 from $120, +42% upside) citing July GPU pricing up 25% across SKUs, short-term contracts at ~3x longer-term rates, and managed inference scaling to >$100M booked ARR in one quarter. Contracted power expanded to 4.2GW; >75% of >$30B exit-2027 ARR target already contracted. UBS also initiates Buy at $120. Long-term margin target raised to ~25–30% by 2030.

bullets.title: AAPL: iPhone 18 Pro lead times softer in China; screenless fitness tracker in development
bullets.body: KeyBanc survey shows iPhone 18 Pro carrier sell-through slightly below iPhone 17 launch; Pro Max lead times ~4 weeks online vs 2-3 weeks for Pro. Apple Store spend +33% YoY launch weekend (+21% in-store, +44% online). Apple separately confirmed to be developing a screenless fitness tracker (Whoop competitor) in early-stage development. Qualcomm renewed global patent license with Apple effective April 2027.

bullets.title: ACN: JPM raises PT to $200; FY27 guidance expected at 1-4% growth, AI disruption headwinds persist
bullets.body: JPM raises ACN Dec-27 PT from $179 to $200, acknowledging 0% organic growth at midpoint vs 2-5% FY27 guidance. F4Q organically +0.7% (vs -3.5% in prior quarter); ~250bps M&A contribution in FY27. ACN-Anthropic AI safety partnership via Faculty acquisition; UBS upgrades to Buy with $275 PT citing expanded AWS collaboration and Accenture Edge midmarket platform with six GA offerings. Stock down ~30% since FY26; consulting segment deteriorating to -4.5% organic.

bullets.title: NOK: Jefferies Buy with €13.80 PT; InP capacity expansion drives 2027-28 EPS 21% above consensus
bullets.body: Jefferies reiterates Buy on Nokia at €9.28 stock, PT €13.80 (+49% upside). Nokia booked ~€5B optical orders from AI since 2025; second San Jose InP fab comes online late 2026 expanding capacity 20x+. Nokia acquiring additional NXP fab. Key product launches in LPO/ELSFP for Scale-Up/Scale-Out. Jefferies 2027-28 EPS forecasts ~21% above consensus. Separately, Seaport Research initiates MRVL with Buy at $270.

bullets.title: RBLX: Hedgeye flips from short to long; bookings trough reached, comps ease into 4Q27
bullets.body: Hedgeye shifted RBLX from short to long as bookings growth decelerated from 70% to guided -14% to -18% in 3Q, marking a trough. Viral hit 'Steal an Egg' reached 14.3M concurrent players; browser-playable games launching by year-end. Comparisons ease sharply in 4Q (lapping 63%, 43%, 8% growth). Citi maintains Buy; 3Q CCU data tracking to $1.67B bookings above guidance of $1.65B.

bullets.title: DIS: raises Disney+ price 13% to $21.49; Guggenheim sees bundling push
bullets.body: Disney raised Disney+ Premium and Hulu Premium by $2.50 each (13%) to $21.49/month but raised the bundle only $2 to $21.99, effectively making the second service nearly free when bundled. Guggenheim sees strategy focused on pushing consumers to bundle rather than standalone subscriptions.

bullets.title: CIEN: Evercore upgrades to Outperform, PT $550; hyper-rail and pump laser bottleneck drive upside
bullets.body: Evercore ISI upgraded CIEN to Outperform from In-Line, raising PT to $550 from $375, projecting 30%+ annual sales growth to $10B+ and $25+ EPS by FY2029. Ciena's 2027 guidance is effectively a supply-floor; Hyper-Rail opportunity concentrated with one hyperscaler but additional wins expected. Pump laser supply remains most constrained; 980nm and 1440nm lead times 12-18 months. At ECOC, CIEN holds majority line system share with no meaningful share shifts expected from CSCO/NOK.
